before.requirement: Process a PRIORITY_UPDATE frame through built-in server reception.
before.reason: The before receive switch has no built-in PRIORITY_UPDATE case; its unknown-extension route ignores the payload. The specific built-in behavior did not yet exist.

after.requirement: Enable built-in PRIORITY_UPDATE reception and submit SETTINGS_NO_RFC7540_PRIORITIES=1 to reach frame processing.
after.reason: The new receive case requires the built-in extension mask and pending no-RFC7540-priorities value of 1. The unchanged constructor uses no option, and the harness submits only MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS, leaving the mask zero and setting the pending value to zero.

claims.reason: The after version adds the built-in receive behavior; there is no corresponding before requirement to compare.

before.requirement: Submit SETTINGS_NO_RFC7540_PRIORITIES=1 so incoming request streams carry the flag required to apply a Priority header.
before.reason: The before Priority-header application guard already requires the stream flag. The harness omits the setting, so pending_no_rfc7540_priorities becomes zero and incoming streams do not acquire the flag.

after.requirement: Submit SETTINGS_NO_RFC7540_PRIORITIES=1 so incoming request streams carry the flag required by the changed guard, which also checks the Priority-header flag.
after.reason: The changed guard retains the stream-flag requirement. The unchanged settings and stream-opening logic leave that flag unset for the fixed harness, so its additional header-flag check cannot make the path reachable.

claims.reason: The same concrete omission of local SETTINGS_NO_RFC7540_PRIORITIES=1 blocks the stream flag on both sides. The diff adds a further guard but does not remove the earlier one.
